In connection with the previous case against Tsang Bing
(章平) alias Tsang Bing Sung (张平生), according to file D.2242,
this person was arrested by the Municipal Police under the latter
name; together with four others named respectively (1) Wong Leu
Ding (王瑞亭)(2)Wong Ming Hun (王民漢)(3)Mo Foh Sung (馬福生) and
(4) Ho Zeu Zang (馬寿仁) in room 29 of the Seward Hotel, (西華旅館)
No.266 East Seward Road whilst holding a communist meeting, during
the evening of April 6 , 1931. The room in question had been
hired by Mo Foh Sung on April 6. Upon appearing before court
the following day, they were extradited to the Chinese
authorities together with the literature seized which included
a proposed draft of a letter of instructions addressed to
"Various Hsiens and Districts in connection with the change
in propaganda work" by the Propaganda Department of the
Kiangsu Branch of the Chinese Communist Party together with
"The Plan of Propaganda Work for May 1". Four of the accused
had arrived in Shanghai from the interior between April 4
and 6, 1931 while the other was a resident of Chapei.
Tabulated statements in Chinese referring to the above
mentioned five accused are appended herewith.

Made/by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross.

Acting on the authority of a warrant of arrest and a
search warrant in respect of a female named Wong Ming Nyi(黃民義)
and premises No. 242 Yates Road, which were issued at the
instance of the Chinese Authorities, the Municipal Police,
accompanied by representatives of the Public Safety Bureau,
raided the aforementioned premises at 5.45 p.m. April 28, 1933.
Nothing of an incriminating nature was found but a male and a
female Chinese named Tseng Bing(章平 ) alias Tsang Bing Sung
(張平生) and Yeng Tsang Sz (楊特氏) were apprehended and
detained at the request of the Public Safety Bureau representatives.

According to the Chinese Authorities the two arrested
persons are active communists and that the female Yang Tsang Sz(楊特氏)
is identical with the Wong Ming Nyi mentioned in the warrant.
Both accused denied being communists. The woman stated that
she had arrived in Shanghai only the day previous from Szechuen
with her infant daughter for the purpose of obtaining medical
treatment for the latter and that prior to her departure for this
city her husband had written to Tsang Bing giving the date of
her arrival in Shanghai and requesting him to arrange
accommodation for her. Tsang Bing, in corroborating the
woman's statement, declared that he had rented the room where
they were arrested, on her behalf the day previous. Questioned
regarding his recent movements the male accused declined to give
any information.

The prisoners appeared before the Second Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court on April 29 when an application for a Writ
of Detention was made by the Police in accordance with the
instructions (copy attached) issued by the D.C. (Crime) on
April 25, 1933. During the proceedings a witness named

依据应中国当局要求签发的针对一名名为黄民义（黃民義）的女性的逮捕令及针对耶茨路（Yates Road）242号房屋的搜查令，工部局警务处在公安局代表的陪同下，于1933年4月28日下午5点45分突袭了上述房屋。未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品，但应公安局代表要求，逮捕并拘留了一男一女两名中国人，分别为曾平（章平），又名张平生（張平生）和杨特氏（楊特氏）。

据中国当局称，这两名被捕者是活跃的共产党员，且女性杨特氏（楊特氏）即为逮捕令中提到的黄民义。两名被告均否认是共产党员。该女子称，她前一天才带着幼女从四川抵达上海，目的是为女儿求医，且在离开前往本市之前，她的丈夫已写信给章平，告知其抵达上海的日期，并请他安排住宿。章平在佐证该女子陈述时声称，他已于前一天代她租下了他们被捕时的房间。当被问及近期的行踪时，男性被告拒绝提供任何信息。

囚犯于4月29日出庭江苏高等法院第二分院，警方根据副警务长（刑事）于1933年4月25日发出的指示（副本附后）申请拘留令。在诉讼过程中，一名名为

statement:-
